answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tax identity itself: every new agent key must pay a compute stamp drawn from a verifiable proof-of-work oracle, and the fee scales with the atlas of already-established identities, so cloning grows costlier as the network matures. An attacker at his profit nadir can afford one or two fakes, but a thousand forked clones would need an orchard of machines burning electricity for nothing, while no honest peer is priced out. Each counterfeit identity thus becomes a guaranteed loss rather than a vote.
